name: Getty Images
description: Read-only Getty Images API v3 access: search the creative and editorial image catalogue by phrase, and read one image's metadata by ID. Metadata only, no downloads and no purchases.

tools.name: search_images
tools.description: Search the Getty Images catalogue by phrase and return image metadata (ID, title, caption, artist, collection, licence model, preview sizes)

asset_family.description: Optional asset family filter: creative (commercial licensing) or editorial (news, sport, entertainment)

tools.name: get_image
tools.description: Get metadata for one Getty Images asset by image ID (title, caption, artist, collection, licence model, dimensions, preview sizes)

image_id.description: Getty Images asset ID, as returned by search_images (e.g. 1234567890)

needs_review: AUTH KEPT AS SCAFFOLDED (header Api-Key), AND NOTHING IN THIS RUN CONTRADICTS IT: Getty's API v3 requires the Api-Key header on every call, which is exactly what services/auth/config/integrationTypeRegistry.js key 'gettyimages' sends in its testHeaders, and that registry form is what this spec reproduces. What the shape-proof below proves: DNS, TLS, base_url, the Api-Key header name and both paths. What it does NOT prove: no Getty credential was held, so a 2xx has never been observed on this connector and neither response pick has been checked against real payload keys.

SOME GETTY SURFACES ALSO WANT AN OAUTH2 BEARER, AND THAT IS OUT OF REACH WITH TODAY'S VAULT FIELDS: Getty documents a client_credentials token exchange (POST /oauth2/token) whose bearer is needed alongside the Api-Key for download, purchase and some restricted metadata. The vault credential declares api_key ONLY, with no client id or secret to exchange, so this connector ships the Api-Key surface and is described as metadata search and read, not as full Getty access. Spec v1.1 could express the combination later (auth oauth2_client_credentials plus static_headers {"Api-Key": "{{api_key}}"}), but only after the vault entry gains the two extra fields; wiring it now would be a false claim, not a head start.

PATHS ARE PROVEN BY THE CONTROL DIFFERENTIAL, NOT BY A GUESS: the control probe at a bogus path on api.gettyimages.com answers 403 {"message":"Missing Authentication Token"} (the API Gateway default), while /v3/search/images and /v3/images/1234567890 both answer 403 {"message":"Forbidden"}. Different error identity at the same status means the routes matched and the rejection came from Getty's own authorizer, so both tool paths are SHAPE_PROVEN.

CLAMPS AND SHAPES REST ON DOCUMENTARY PROVENANCE: page_size is clamped to a default of 30 and a maximum of 100 per Getty's documented paging limits, and the asset_family and sort_order enums are the documented value sets. The response picks follow the documented v3 envelopes (search returns result_count plus images[]; the single-image read returns images[] plus images_not_found), so an unexpected key would silently pick nothing rather than error. Both are worth re-checking on the first 2xx with a real key.

PROBE VALUES ARE HARMLESS AND READ-ONLY: _probe supplies phrase 'mountain', asset_family 'creative', sort_order 'best_match' and image_id '1234567890' so the blind harness can route a search and an identifier path. The image ID is a placeholder digit string, not a known asset, and with a dummy key the call never reaches asset lookup anyway. Credentials are never hinted, and _probe sits at TOOL level because the harness reads tool._probe and ignores one nested inside request.
READ-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION: both tools are GET metadata reads. Getty's download, purchase and asset-management routes are deliberately absent, and no tool here can spend a Getty download credit.
